technique.name: Jab
technique.description: A rapid lead-hand linear strike designed to reach a target through an efficient path while preserving structural alignment, balance, defensive coverage, mobility, and rapid recovery.

steps.goal: Build a balanced guard before the punch begins.
key_cues: Keep both elbows softly bent near 90 degrees.
Keep both hands closed and ready.
steps.why_it_matters: A stable guard gives the jab a repeatable start and a safe position to return to.
steps.transition_condition: Hold both elbow angles between 70 and 110 degrees with at least 65% body coverage for 1.2 seconds.

non_angle_features.label: Rear fist is chambered and controlled

steps.goal: Send the lead fist directly to useful reach while the rear hand protects.
key_cues: Drive the fist straight toward the target.
Reach 155 to 177 degrees at the lead elbow.
Stop short of locking the elbow.
Keep the rear hand near guard.
steps.why_it_matters: Controlled extension creates reach without sacrificing the elbow or the defensive guard.
steps.transition_condition: Reach a lead-elbow angle of 155 to 177 degrees with at least 65% body coverage, then hold the controlled position for 1.2 seconds.

body_evidence.label: Hips remain balanced in front stance

steps.goal: Retract the lead hand promptly and rebuild the original guard.
key_cues: Bring the lead fist back on the same direct path.
Restore the lead elbow to 70 to 110 degrees.
Keep both fists closed and the stance balanced.
steps.why_it_matters: The recovery limits exposure and prepares the next action.
avoid: Letting the lead hand drift downward
steps.transition_condition: Restore the lead-elbow angle to 70 to 110 degrees with at least 65% body coverage and hold guard for 1.2 seconds.

body_evidence.label: Front stance remains stable through recovery

measurement_policy.movement_style: Karate straight punch from front stance
measurement_policy.measurement_reason: Camera-plane arm flexion avoids monocular depth bending; torso and lower-body angles retain world-space depth.
measurement_policy.primary: Used for step scoring and temporal phase evidence
measurement_policy.supporting: Used for live coaching and target-shape guidance
measurement_policy.missing_supporting_data: Reduce confidence; do not reject the repetition

overview.summary: A rapid lead-hand linear strike designed to reach a target through an efficient path while preserving structural alignment, balance, defensive coverage, mobility, and rapid recovery.
objectives: Move the lead hand toward the target with minimal unnecessary displacement.
Use a direct, efficient hand path with limited lateral deviation.
Keep the non-striking hand in its defensive reference position.
Keep the center of mass supported by a controllable base.
Preserve mobility and readiness for another action.
Avoid unnecessary tension, overextension, and joint loading.
Return efficiently to a defensively useful state.
safety: Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm.
Do not forcefully lock the elbow at full extension.
Practise with clear space and controlled speed.
Prioritize safety, balance, defensive coverage, then efficiency.

principles.title: Direct hand path
principles.explanation: The lead fist travels forward with minimal unnecessary sideways movement. A shorter path generally makes the action easier to control and retract.

principles.title: Controlled elbow extension
principles.explanation: The elbow extends behind the fist while remaining short of a forceful lock. The wrist, elbow, and shoulder should support the direction of the strike.

principles.title: Stable base
principles.explanation: The stance supports the movement while the torso stays controlled. Reaching with the upper body can move the body beyond its comfortable base of support.

principles.title: Coordinated movement
principles.explanation: The fist, elbow, shoulder, torso, and stance contribute as a sequence rather than as isolated parts. The goal is efficient timing, not unnecessary tension.

principles.title: Immediate recovery
principles.explanation: After extension, the fist returns along a controlled path and the guard is restored. Recovery is part of the technique, not an action added afterward.

principles.title: How to interpret force
principles.explanation: Punching force depends on mass, acceleration, timing, contact, and whole-body coordination. A camera can describe visible motion but does not directly measure impact force or joint torque.

principles.title: Biomechanics
principles.explanation: The body segments work together to produce and control the strike. Reference positions are variables that support functional goals.

principles.title: Stability
principles.explanation: A stable base resists unwanted loss of control while preserving the ability to move again.

principles.title: Mobility
principles.explanation: A useful position leaves enough freedom to evade, continue, defend, or change direction.

principles.title: Defensive coverage
principles.explanation: The non-striking side and body position should limit unnecessary exposed area while the striking limb is committed.

principles.title: Exposure
principles.explanation: Exposure is the vulnerable area and duration created by the movement. Efficient technique limits both.

principles.title: Energy efficiency
principles.explanation: A useful solution avoids unnecessary tension, wind-up, and body displacement.

principles.title: Joint safety
principles.explanation: Useful reach is preferred over maximum possible extension so the joints remain controlled and recovery stays available.

principles.title: Temporal efficiency
principles.explanation: Each phase should happen in a useful sequence, with recovery beginning promptly after peak reach.
